question: Why is the Lord asked to declare his own powerful sovereignty within the hymn?
premises: The hymn concerns the Lord’s own lordship.
The Lord is mighty and powerful.
The speaker requests the Lord to speak of it.
inference: The Lord alone is fit to declare his own powerful sovereignty in the hymn.
uncertainties: The accusative prabhāviṇam may qualify svāmitām or īśvaraṃ; syntax is compressed.
plain_english: O Lord, O mighty one, you should declare your own powerful lordship in this hymn.
